complexity_scope.guarantee: For every covered algorithm there exists one fixed hard objective giving the displayed deterministic gap.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: c0,d0 universal; the source gives conservative c0=2^(-24) after increasing the dimension threshold. Error constant 2^(-17) and eta are explicit.
complexity_scope.oracle: At time t a deterministic Borel map Q_t:(X x R)^(t-1)->X chooses x_t from the exact history (x_i,f(x_i)); a Borel Q_out:(X x R)^T->X returns any feasible point, which need not have been queried. The unknown objective is fixed. Only exact scalar f(x) is returned; arbitrary exact-real internal computation is free. Repeated oracle calls count; reuse of an already stored value makes no new call.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Any Borel terminal xhat in X, queried or unqueried; lower bound on absolute function gap F(xhat)-min F.
complexity_scope.regime: T<dm/8 and the displayed integer/dimension conditions.
complexity_scope.resource: Exact scalar function-value calls; arbitrary exact-real internal computation uncharged. A reused cached value costs no new call.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: All deterministic adaptive Borel feasible-query/output policies; fixed horizon T, or pathwise bounded early stopping padded by ignored repeated calls.

content.intended_use: Convert a bounded deterministic exact-value query budget into objective error; retain the cubic dimension constraint.

proofs.locator: Lemmas 6.1–6.5; Lemma 7.1/Corollary 7.2; Section 8; Propositions 9.1,10.1,10.2,11.1; proof of Theorem 3.4
map: Use R0=R/4, rho=R/(256m^(3/2)), A=beta rho/8, eta=beta/(4096m^2); F_U=A h_(m,rho)(U^T x)+(beta/8)dist(x,B(R0))^2+(eta/2)||x||^2. Lemma 6.1 supplies 0<=g-h<=rho/4, ||grad h||<=1, Lip(grad h)<=2/rho. These use standard Moreau calculus as an imported source interface; its cited book is not separately read.

For d>=8, b=floor(d/4)>=d/8, so T<dm/8 implies T<bm. Section 8 chooses a frame after each completed block using cap avoidance. Lemma 7.1 proves existence via Gaussian/spherical concentration and a union bound; Corollary 7.2 validates p>=d/2, M<=d^2/16+1 using m^3 log(ed)<=c0 d. The cited concentration reference is not independently rederived here.

Lemma 6.3 gives exact prefix equality. Proposition 9.1 applies it at every complete/incomplete-block query and inducts through the deterministic policy, realizing the entire transcript by one final F_U. The sentinel is orthogonal to xhat and all later directions are rho-small there, giving i_rho^+(U^T xhat)<=q+1<=m.

Proposition 10.1 bounds Lip(grad F_U)<=beta/4+beta/4+eta<beta. The quadratic ensures coercivity and eta-strong convexity. On a unit v perpendicular to range(U), |t|<=R0 gives F_U(tv)=A h(0)+(eta/2)t^2, so no larger global modulus is possible.
Proposition 10.2 uses the first-order condition outside B(R0): 0>=-A+(beta/4)(r-R0)+eta r. Thus r<=R0+4A/beta=R0+rho/2<R/2.

Lemma 6.5 gives h(U^T xhat)-h(ycirc)>=3R0/(4sqrt(m)) for ycirc=-(R0/sqrt(m))1_m. At xcirc=U ycirc the radial penalty vanishes. Proposition 11.1 obtains gap >=A*3R0/(4sqrt(m))-(eta/2)R0^2=11 beta R^2/(2^17 m^2)>=2^(-17) beta R^2/m^2.
proofs.omitted_details: This is a precise source-linked proof map, not full independent reproof or formal verification. Standard Moreau/projection calculus and Gaussian concentration are imported as identified above; external references were not separately read.
proofs.reading_coverage: Statements pp.6–7, chain/dual pp.12–14, gap/cap pp.15–16, compiler pp.16–17, consistency pp.18, admissibility pp.18–19 and terminal proof p.20 were read from this selected PDF or registered derivatives.

assumptions: All query and terminal maps are feasible Borel maps on every transcript, as in Section 3.1.
The chain length satisfies 1<=m<=d/4 and m^3 log(ed)<=c0 d.
statement.conclusion: F(xhat)-F^*>=2^(-17) beta R^2/m^2. The constructed F has global strong-convexity modulus exactly eta=beta/(4096 m^2), globally Lipschitz gradient with constant strictly less than beta, and unique global minimizer of norm <R/2.
statement.objects_and_definitions: X=B_2^d(R), C=B_2^d(R/2). F_beta(d,R) consists of convex C^1 functions f:R^d->R with globally beta-Lipschitz gradient in Euclidean norm and a unique global minimizer x_f^* in C; f^*=min_R^d f. At time t a deterministic Borel map Q_t:(X x R)^(t-1)->X chooses x_t from the exact history (x_i,f(x_i)); a Borel Q_out:(X x R)^T->X returns any feasible point, which need not have been queried. The unknown objective is fixed. Only exact scalar f(x) is returned; arbitrary exact-real internal computation is free. Repeated oracle calls count; reuse of an already stored value makes no new call.
statement.parameter_domains: d,m integers; d>=d0 (increased to at least 8); R,beta>0; 1<=m<=d/4; m^3 log(ed)<=c0 d; T in N_0, T<dm/8.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal c0>0 and d0 in N such that for every d>=d0, every R,beta>0, every admissible integer m and every deterministic adaptive policy with integer budget T<dm/8, there exists a single fixed F in F_beta(d,R), depending on that policy, for which the stated gap holds. No probability or randomized-policy claim.

use_restrictions: The lower bound covers deterministic adaptive Borel policies with bounded queries and output; it is not a randomized, unrestricted-query, C^2/C^infinity or fixed-condition-number lower bound.
Source-linked long proof; no independent reproof of cited concentration or Moreau literature is claimed. Strong convexity varies with m.
